_podcast.theme_scoring_prompt: Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Wild Spaces & Outdoor Life' through a RURAL TECH AND INNOVATION lens. Strong fits include: wildfire detection tech and BC Wildfire monitoring systems, satellite/drone surveillance for Chilcotin wilderness, wildlife tracking and conservation technology, watershed sensors and salmon habitat monitoring, weather stations and climate tracking in backcountry, avalanche forecasting tech, trail mapping and GPS systems, outdoor recreation apps and connectivity, backcountry communication devices (satellite messengers, Meshtastic), flood/drought prediction systems, remote cameras for wildlife research, and how technology helps manage and protect Cariboo wild spaces. Prefer articles that bridge wilderness/conservation AND technology. Penalise heavily (score 0–20): prehistoric and ancient biology (fossils, palaeontology, deep-time creatures) with no contemporary conservation technology angle — these belong to Sunday's Science theme; AI and data centre infrastructure stories about business strategy, investment, or corporate politics rather than direct wilderness, ecosystem, or land-use impact in BC; geopolitical conflict, war, and crime news with no outdoor or conservation relevance; consumer tech reviews and financial market stories; general political and judicial news. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Quebec separatist Parti Québécois wins minority government, reviving referendum drive
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

The Parti Québécois won 59 of 127 seats in Quebec’s Oct. 5 election, returning to power under leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon but falling five seats short of the 64 needed for a majority. The Liberals won 40 seats, the Conservatives 19 and Québec solidaire nine. The Coalition Avenir Québec, which had governed for eight years, won none. The PQ received about 28% of the vote [castanet.net#1][cbc.ca#1][lapresse.ca#1]. St-Pierre Plamondon reiterated his call for a referendum on Quebec sovereignty but said he would wait until U.S. President Donald Trump’s term ends in 2029. As a minority government, the PQ will need opposition support to pass legislation and survive confidence votes. St-Pierre Plamondon said voters had asked the party to work with other parties [wral.com#1][cbc.ca#2][bbc.co.uk#1][dw.com#1]. The PQ’s platform includes cutting government spending by $6.6 billion over five years, reducing immigration and changing health-care administration. Prime Minister Mark Carney congratulated St-Pierre Plamondon and said building a stronger Quebec is central to building a stronger Canada [cbc.ca#2][perthnow.com.au#1].

items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

A Millennium Cross-Section on a Living Street — This project originates from a major breakthrough in the archaeological discovery and conservation practice at Bastion No. 11 of the Jingzhou City Wall. Since 2016, this section of the ancient wall had been listed for emergency conservation due to foundation settlement and structural cracking. During the repair process, a stratified structure of "walls built upon walls," spanning the Five Dynasties, Song, Ming, and Qing periods, was uncovered. This led to the approval by the National Cultural Heritage Administration for systematic archaeological excavation.
